title: Talent absorption 12-week experiment retrospective
content:
Summary

This note is a retrospective for the 12-week 'talent absorption' experiment run by People Ops (Aug 2025–Sep 2025). The experiment bundled three levers: faster funnel triage, simplified rubric scoring, and a micro-onboard pathway for the first 14 days. Goal: reduce median time-to-productivity (TTP) for IC engineers from hire -> first independent PR from ~42 days to <= 21 days while keeping candidate quality stable.

Hypotheses we tested

- H1: Condensing structured interviews to 3 focused probes (systems design, debugging, and async communication) with calibrated artifacts reduces interview cycle time without increasing post-hire quality regressions.
- H2: A 14-day micro-onboard (day0-day14 checklist + 3 small shipped tasks) lowers TTP and improves new-hire confidence scores.
- H3: A 'warm-handoff' between recruiter and hiring manager with a 30-minute alignment sync reduces acceptance friction and onboarding information gaps.

Design and runbook (experiment plan)

1) Funnel changes (recruiting flow)
- Phone screen -> Take-home (2hr) -> Onsite (3 probes, 2.5 hrs total). Removed redundant architectural whiteboard tasks.
- Time-box: target 8 business days from phone screen to onsite invite. Recruiter cadence template: 48h follow-up increments.
- Candidate communications: single-page expectation doc sent at phone screen stage (what interviewers evaluate, sample rubric excerpt, onboarding preview).

2) Interview rubric (simplified, shared with interviewers)
- 3 pillars scored 1-5: Impact (does work move product forward), Craft (technical correctness & tradeoffs), Communication (clarity, async writing).
- Passing threshold: median >= 3.5 and no pillar < 3.
- Calibration: weekly 30-min panel calibrations during the experiment. Interviewers used anchor examples (github snippets) to align scoring.

3) Micro-onboard (first 14 days)
- Pre-day0: access checklist (VPN, laptop image, repos) completed by IT within 48 hours of offer acceptance.
- Day0–2: orientation + tiny task (edit docs, run local infra).
- Day3–7: shadowing + assigned 2 small bugs/features with mentor pair. Goal: ship a PR by EOW.
- Day8–14: independent owner of a tiny backlog slice (bug triage + minor change). Weekly syncs with mentor; retro at day 14.
- Measurement: first merged PR by day14, self-rated confidence 1–5 at day14.

4) Acceptance & warm-handoff
- Once offer verbally accepted, recruiter schedules 30-min warm-handoff call: hiring manager + recruiter + future mentor (if identified) to align role expectations, ramp map, and immediate first tasks. Follow-up email with 3 immediate onboarding goals.

Signals and metrics tracked

- Recruiting KPIs: time from phone-screen -> offer, offer-to-acceptance time, offer acceptance rate, onsite-to-offer conversion.
- Quality & ramp KPIs: median days to first merged PR, manager-rated 30-day effectiveness, new-hire self-rated confidence (day14), early retention (30-day).
- Interview quality: percentage of hires flagged for performance remediation in first 90 days.

Outcomes (what we observed)

- Time reductions: median phone-screen -> offer dropped 23% (from 18d -> 13.8d). Offer-to-accept averaged 3.6 days (unchanged). Overall time-to-offer improved but conversion rates vary.
- Ramp: median days to first merged PR improved from 42 -> 19 (target achieved). 62% of hires shipped a first PR within 14 days (baseline ~18%).
- Quality: manager-rated 30-day effectiveness averaged 3.6/5 vs baseline 3.7 (no statistically significant drop given small sample N=28). 90-day remediation flags remained flat (2/28).
- Candidate experience: Net Promoter-ish comments improved in post-hire survey; candidates appreciated the expectation doc and warm-handoff clarity.

Observations and qualitative notes

- The simplified rubric reduced interviewer fatigue and decreased calibration variance but required upfront training (anchor examples) — skip the training and scores drift.
- The micro-onboard heavily depends on mentor bandwidth and pre-offer access provisioning. Failed cases correlated with slow IT access and mentors overloaded.
- Some hiring managers reported initial anxiety about fewer interview probes; however, when combined with high-fidelity take-homes, confidence in hires remained high.

Failure modes we logged

- IT provisioning delays (VPN, repo perms) caused 4 hires to miss day0 tasks and delayed shipping beyond day14.
- Mentor overload: mentors assigned to >2 new hires concurrently had lower follow-through, leading to worse outcomes.
- Take-home variance: some take-homes were not well-calibrated for role seniority; leads to over/underestimate of candidate suitability.

Recommendations (next steps)

- Operational: negotiate a 48-hour SLA with IT for post-accept provisioning. Create a lightweight escalation path (ops ticket + people-ops on-call) for any delay >48h.
- Mentorship: formalize 'mentor capacity' (max 2 direct mentees onboarding concurrently) and create a small mentor stipend/recognition program.
- Rubric: keep 3-pillar rubric but expand anchor bank and record 4 short calibration videos for interviewers. Make calibration part of interviewer onboarding.
- Take-homes: standardize 2 templates (junior / senior) and require reviewer notes + time estimate. Provide anonymized sample solutions for calibration.
- Rollout: expand to two additional roles (SRE, Product Data) for Q4 pilot, measure N>=60 hires before finalizing.

Action items (owners & timeline)

- IT SLA proposal: Priya Raman by 2025-10-10.
- Mentor capacity & recognition draft: Miguel Torres by 2025-10-15.
- Rubric anchor bank + calibration vids: Samir Gupta + Eve Johnson by 2025-10-20.
- Take-home templates and reviewer guide: Hiring committee by 2025-10-12.

Appendix: practical onboarding checklist (copyable)

Pre-offer acceptance (recommended)
- Recruiter: confirm manager preference on mentor (Y/N) and list of repos.
- IT: verify provisioning runbook exists for role.

Immediate post-accept (0–48h)
- IT: laptop image + VPN + repo perms assigned.
- Recruiter: send single-page "What to expect in week 0–2" doc and calendar invites (orient, mentor syncs).
- Manager: 30-min warm-handoff with recruiter + mentor.

Day0–2\- Orientation: company rituals, infra quickstarts, run local services.
- Tiny task: follow single documented guide and open initial PR (doc update, lint fix).

Day3–7\- Pair on 2 small tickets; mentor reviews; ship first PR.
- Weekly check-in: 30-min manager + mentor + new hire.

Day8–14\- Independent ownership of 1–2 micro-tasks and a retrospective with mentor.
- Day14: confidence survey + first-14-day retro notes in shared folder.

Closing note

This experiment showed promising improvements in ramp speed without clear short-term quality regressions, but it requires disciplined operations and mentor resourcing to scale. If we adopt these changes, we should treat provisioning SLAs and mentor capacity as first-class constraints in hiring forecasts.
